headline: US stocks bounced at Monday's open but crypto did not follow: bitcoin hovered near $74,500 and ether was down about 4%, while Strategy kept buying bitcoin below its own average cost.

market.asOf: Read from CoinDesk at 10:50am ET (15:50 UTC, 22:50 Bangkok) Mon 9 Nov; SOL from CoinDesk's price ticker at about 16:05 UTC. CoinGecko could not be opened this run. Use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: Not confirmed this run: the Fear & Greed index page could not be opened.

stories.title: Stocks bounce at the open, crypto doesn't
stories.summary: The Nasdaq was up 2.5% at 10:50am ET even with Nvidia down 4%, but bitcoin was still down 0.65% over 24 hours at about $74,480, and ether and XRP were each down about 4%, per CoinDesk. Nvidia's board is investigating CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an executive suspected of working for Chinese intelligence; crypto had sold off over the weekend on that news and on failed Iran talks.
points: Bitcoin fell to about $73,761 late Sunday, its lowest since August; CoinDesk names the 200-day average near $73,150 as support and the 100-day average near $77,430 as resistance.
Liquidations topped $1B in 24 hours, per CoinDesk citing CoinGlass ($913M of it bets on higher prices); a separate CoinDesk count puts the total at $1.16B with about $500M in ether.
Ether closed Sunday below its 200-day average for the first time since 18 Aug, per CoinDesk.
Bitcoin's one-week implied volatility rose to about 43% from about 33%, and four of its six most-traded options were $70,000-$72,000 puts (bets on further falls), per CoinDesk.
Nvidia lost more than $250B in market value at one point, while Alphabet rose 3.4% on its AI-chip push, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: Strategy buys 1,036 more bitcoin but stays below its average cost; MSCI decides Wednesday
stories.summary: Strategy (MSTR) bought 1,036 BTC for $81.9M last week at about $79,012 each, per its 9 Nov SEC filing. It now holds 850,364 BTC at an average cost of $75,456, so with bitcoin near $74,800 the stake was about 0.9% under water on paper, per Bitcoin Magazine. On Wednesday MSCI says whether Strategy stays in its stock indexes.
points: Strategy paid for the purchase by selling 2,051,348 MSTR shares for $283.8M, and also spent $188.3M buying back its STRC preferred shares, per the filing.
MSCI announces its review at 5:00pm ET Wed 11 Nov; any removals take effect at the close on 30 Nov, per TechTimes.
US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $1.282B last week, the largest weekly outflow since late June, leaving 2026 flows at about -$914M, per CoinDesk citing SoSoValue.

stories.title: Wall Street keeps building on crypto rails: NYSE picks Avalanche, Coinbase gets a federal trust charter
stories.summary: The New York Stock Exchange will use the Avalanche blockchain to clear and settle trades on its planned tokenized-stock venue, which aims to trade around the clock if regulators approve, per CoinDesk; no launch date was given. Separately, the OCC gave final approval to Coinbase National Trust Company, per Decrypt.
points: AVAX rose 8% over 24 hours on the NYSE news, per CoinDesk.
Coinbase says the charter does not make it a commercial bank and it will not take retail deposits, per Decrypt.
Circle and Ripple already hold final OCC approvals; a community bankers' group is suing the OCC over these charters, per Decrypt.
Schwab clients can now trade SOL, AVAX and LINK, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Binance hack fallout continues
briefs.summary: HYPE and APT withdrawals are back; Binance has pledged to restore INJ, PLASMA, NEAR and LTC by the end of this week. CryptoQuant data shows BTC on Binance down about 7.7% since the hack, with outflows slowing.

briefs.title: North Korea moving Binance loot through homemade memecoins
briefs.summary: Elliptic found at least six NEAR memecoins used to move about 117,000 NEAR; about 11.8M NEAR has not moved yet.

briefs.title: Ankr bridge drained
briefs.summary: Five forged withdrawals took about $304,500, per CoinInsider; withdrawals were paused at 09:51 UTC.
